entries.definition: A person who has reached the age when they are legally or fully grown; or relating to grown people rather than children.
entries.definitionZh: 成年人；成年的；成人的
examples: An adult must accompany the children.
The event is intended for an adult audience.
entries.tip: The legal age of adulthood differs between countries and for different legal purposes.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a grown person or describe something intended for grown people.

senses.definition: A person who is fully grown, especially one who has reached the legally recognised age of adulthood.
senses.definitionZh: 已经完全长大的人，尤指达到法律认可成年年龄的人；成年人。
examples: Each child must be with an adult.
The museum offers separate tickets for adults and children.

senses.definition: Fully grown, or intended for people who are fully grown.
senses.definitionZh: 已经成年的；或专为成年人设计或提供的。
examples: She is an adult learner returning to school.
The film is suitable for an adult audience.

entries.definition: A person in your family who lived a long time before you, such as a great-grandparent.
entries.definitionZh: 祖先；祖辈；先人
examples: One of her ancestors came from Italy.
The family keeps records of its ancestors.
entries.tip: An ancestor is someone from an earlier generation; a descendant is someone from a later generation.
entries.breakdown: Refers to a person from an earlier generation in a family line.

senses.definition: A person in your family who lived in an earlier generation, often many years ago.
senses.definitionZh: 家族中生活在更早一代的人，通常指许多年前的祖辈；祖先。
examples: Her ancestors lived in the countryside.
He researched his ancestors using old letters.

entries.definition: The sister of your mother or father, or the wife of your uncle.
entries.definitionZh: 姑母；姨母；伯母；婶婶；舅母；阿姨
examples: My aunt lives near the beach.
We visited our aunt during the school holidays.
entries.tip: The exact Chinese family term depends on whether the aunt is related through the mother or father and on family age relationships.
entries.breakdown: A family relationship term for a parent's sister or an uncle's wife.

senses.definition: The sister of someone's mother or father, or the wife of someone's uncle.
senses.definitionZh: 某人的母亲或父亲的姐妹，或叔叔、舅舅等的妻子；姑母、姨母或阿姨等。
examples: My aunt taught me how to bake.
Her aunt and uncle came to the wedding.

entries.definition: A very young child who has not yet learned to walk or talk; or the youngest or smallest member of a group.
entries.definitionZh: 婴儿；宝宝；家庭或群体中最年幼的成员。
examples: The baby is sleeping in the cot.
He is the baby of the family.
entries.tip: The plural is “babies”. “Baby” can be used informally as a term of affection, depending on context.
entries.breakdown: Usually means an infant, but can also describe the youngest member of a family or group.

senses.definition: A very young child, especially one who is not yet able to walk or speak.
senses.definitionZh: 非常年幼的孩子，尤指尚未学会走路或说话的婴儿。
examples: The baby began to cry.
They bought a car seat for their new baby.

senses.definition: The youngest or smallest member of a family or group.
senses.definitionZh: 家庭或群体中年龄最小或体型最小的成员。
examples: He is the baby of the family.
The new player is the baby of the team.

entries.definition: A male partner in a romantic relationship; or, in some contexts, a male friend.
entries.definitionZh: 男朋友；男性伴侣；男性朋友（较少见）
examples: She introduced her boyfriend to her parents.
My boyfriend and I enjoy hiking.
entries.tip: In everyday modern use, “boyfriend” usually means a romantic partner, not simply a male friend.
entries.breakdown: Usually describes a person's male romantic partner.

senses.definition: A man or boy who is in a romantic relationship with someone.
senses.definitionZh: 与某人处于恋爱关系的男性；男朋友。
examples: Her boyfriend gave her flowers.
They have been boyfriend and girlfriend for two years.

senses.definition: A male friend, especially in older or less common usage where the romantic meaning is not intended.
senses.definitionZh: 男性朋友，尤指较旧或较少见的用法中不表示恋爱关系时。
examples: She invited a boyfriend from school to the event.
He was one of her closest boyfriends.

entries.definition: A woman who is getting married or has recently married.
entries.definitionZh: 新娘
examples: The bride arrived at the ceremony with her father.
The bride and groom thanked their guests.
entries.tip: The male partner getting married is the “groom”.
entries.breakdown: Refers to the woman at the centre of a wedding ceremony or newly married woman.

senses.definition: A woman on her wedding day or a woman who has recently married.
senses.definitionZh: 在婚礼当天结婚的女性，或刚刚结婚的女性；新娘。
examples: The bride wore a simple white dress.
Guests waited for the bride to enter.

entries.definition: A boy or man who has the same parent or parents as another person; or a man who shares a close group, belief, or community with others.
entries.definitionZh: 兄弟；哥哥；弟弟；同胞；兄弟会成员
examples: My brother works in another city.
She has two older brothers.
entries.tip: English “brother” does not show whether the person is older or younger; Chinese uses different words for older and younger brothers.
entries.breakdown: A family relationship term; context can also extend it to people sharing a community or organisation.

senses.definition: A male person who has one or both parents in common with another person.
senses.definitionZh: 与另一个人有一个或两个共同父母的男性；兄弟、哥哥或弟弟。
examples: My younger brother is still at school.
Her brother helped her move house.

senses.definition: A man who belongs to the same religious, social, or professional group as others, or who is treated as a close companion.
senses.definitionZh: 属于同一宗教、社会或职业团体的男性成员，或被视为亲密伙伴的男性。
examples: The monks called one another brother.
He regarded his teammates as brothers.

entries.definition: A friend or companion, especially one you do an activity with; an informal way to address someone.
entries.definitionZh: 伙伴；朋友；搭档；老兄（非正式称呼）
examples: He went fishing with his old buddy.
Thanks for your help, buddy.
entries.tip: “Buddy” is informal and common in North American English; use more neutral terms in formal situations.
entries.breakdown: A friendly, informal word for someone you know or spend time with.

senses.definition: A friend or companion, often someone you spend time or do activities with.
senses.definitionZh: 朋友或伙伴，通常指一起相处或参加活动的人。
examples: I am meeting a buddy after work.
He has been my fishing buddy for years.

senses.definition: An informal way of speaking directly to someone, especially in a friendly or familiar tone.
senses.definitionZh: 直接称呼某人的非正式说法，尤指友好或熟悉的语气。
examples: Hey, buddy, how are you?
Listen, buddy, I need your help.

entries.definition: A person who legally belongs to a particular country and has the rights and responsibilities of that country.
entries.definitionZh: 公民；国民；市民
examples: Every citizen has responsibilities as well as rights.
The programme helps young citizens understand local government.
entries.tip: A citizen is a legal member of a country; a resident may live there without being a citizen.
entries.breakdown: Usually refers to legal membership of a country, although it can also mean a person living in a particular city.

senses.definition: A person who has legal membership of a country and is entitled to its rights and subject to its laws.
senses.definitionZh: 依法属于某个国家、享有该国权利并承担相应法律义务的人；公民或国民。
examples: The law protects every citizen.
She became a citizen after completing the required process.

senses.definition: A person who lives in a particular town or city, especially when discussing public life and responsibilities.
senses.definitionZh: 居住在某个城镇或城市的人，尤指讨论公共生活和责任时；市民。
examples: The mayor met with local citizens.
Citizens can attend the public meeting.

entries.definition: A person who is in the same class or study group as you at school or another educational institution.
entries.definitionZh: 同班同学；同学
examples: I worked with a classmate on the science project.
She has known her classmates since primary school.
entries.tip: A classmate is in the same class; a schoolmate may attend the same school but be in a different class.
entries.breakdown: A school or study relationship based on being in the same class.

senses.definition: A person who studies in the same class or teaching group as another person.
senses.definitionZh: 与另一个人在同一个班级或教学小组学习的人；同班同学。
examples: My classmate lent me a pencil.
The teacher asked each classmate to introduce themselves.

entries.definition: A child of your aunt or uncle; a relative who shares a more distant family connection.
entries.definitionZh: 堂兄弟姐妹；表兄弟姐妹；堂亲；表亲
examples: My cousin is visiting us this weekend.
She has several cousins on her mother's side.
entries.tip: English “cousin” does not specify gender or whether the relative is older or younger; Chinese kinship terms are more specific.
entries.breakdown: A family term for the child of an aunt or uncle, regardless of gender.

senses.definition: A child of someone's aunt or uncle, whether male or female.
senses.definitionZh: 某人的姑母、姨母、叔伯或舅舅等的子女，不区分性别；堂亲或表亲。
examples: My cousin lives in Penang.
He invited all his cousins to the family gathering.

entries.definition: Two people or things considered together, especially two people in a romantic relationship; or to join two things together.
entries.definitionZh: 一对；夫妻；情侣；几个；连接；结合
examples: The couple moved into a new apartment.
A couple of friends are coming over.
entries.tip: “A couple of” often means two, but informally it can mean a small number.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to two people or items, a romantic pair, or the act of joining things.

senses.definition: Two people who are married or in a romantic relationship.
senses.definitionZh: 已婚或处于恋爱关系的两个人；夫妻或情侣。
examples: The couple celebrated their anniversary.
A young couple sat near the window.

senses.definition: Two people or things considered together; in informal use, a small number.
senses.definitionZh: 被视为一组的两个人或两个事物；非正式用法中也可表示少量。
examples: I need a couple of minutes.
She bought a couple of notebooks.

senses.definition: To connect or join two things together.
senses.definitionZh: 将两个事物连接或结合在一起。
examples: The railway lines are coupled together.
The two events are closely coupled.

entries.definition: A female child in relation to her parents.
entries.definitionZh: 女儿
examples: Their daughter starts school next year.
My daughter enjoys drawing and reading.
entries.tip: The male equivalent is “son”.
entries.breakdown: A direct family relationship term for a female child.

senses.definition: A female child in relation to one or both of her parents.
senses.definitionZh: 相对于父母而言的女性子女；女儿。
examples: Their youngest daughter lives nearby.
He is proud of his daughter's work.

entries.definition: A person who lives near you; or to be next to or close to something.
entries.definitionZh: 邻居；邻近的人；与……相邻
examples: Our neighbours are very friendly.
The two villages neighbour each other.
entries.tip: British English spells the word “neighbour”; American English uses “neighbor”.
entries.breakdown: Usually a person living nearby; the verb is less common and means to be next to something.

senses.definition: A person who lives near another person or household.
senses.definitionZh: 住在某人或某户人家附近的人；邻居。
examples: We invited our neighbours to dinner.
A neighbour helped us carry the boxes.

senses.definition: To be located next to or close to another place or area.
senses.definitionZh: 位于另一个地点或区域旁边或附近；与……相邻。
examples: The park neighbours the school.
Their property neighbours a large field.

entries.definition: A person, group, or country that opposes or wants to harm another; or something harmful that must be overcome.
entries.definitionZh: 敌人；仇敌；有害因素；大敌
examples: The two countries were once enemies.
Lack of sleep is the enemy of concentration.
entries.tip: An enemy is someone or something opposed to you; an opponent may simply be someone competing against you.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a hostile person or group, or figuratively to a harmful force or condition.

senses.definition: A person, group, or country that is actively opposed to another or may try to harm them.
senses.definitionZh: 积极反对他人或可能试图伤害他人的个人、群体或国家；敌人。
examples: The soldiers faced the enemy across the river.
They became enemies after the argument.

senses.definition: Something that causes damage or makes success more difficult.
senses.definitionZh: 造成损害或使成功变得更加困难的事物；大敌。
examples: Stress can be an enemy of good health.
Carelessness is the enemy of accuracy.

entries.definition: A person or animal that belongs to the sex that can produce eggs or give birth; or relating to that sex.
entries.definitionZh: 女性；雌性；女性的；雌性的
examples: The study included both male and female participants.
The female bird builds the nest.
entries.tip: “Female” is often used in scientific, official, or statistical contexts; “woman” is usually more natural when referring to an adult person.
entries.breakdown: A biological or demographic term that can function as a noun or adjective.

senses.definition: A person or animal of the sex that produces eggs or, in many species, gives birth.
senses.definitionZh: 属于能够产生卵子或在许多物种中能够生育这一性别的人或动物；雌性或女性。
examples: The survey included fifty females and fifty males.
The female of this species is larger.

senses.definition: Relating to the sex that produces eggs or gives birth.
senses.definitionZh: 与能够产生卵子或生育的性别有关的；女性的或雌性的。
examples: The female athletes trained together.
A female elephant was caring for the calf.

entries.definition: A man who is polite, considerate, and well-mannered; or a formal and polite way to refer to a man.
entries.definitionZh: 绅士；有礼貌的男士；先生
examples: He behaved like a true gentleman.
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the event.
entries.tip: The plural is “gentlemen”. It can sound formal or old-fashioned in some everyday situations.
entries.breakdown: Often describes a man's polite behaviour or serves as a formal form of address.

senses.definition: A man who behaves politely, respectfully, and considerately toward others.
senses.definitionZh: 举止礼貌、尊重他人并体贴周到的男性；绅士。
examples: He offered his seat to the older passenger like a gentleman.
A gentleman always treats others with respect.

senses.definition: A polite or formal way of referring to a man, especially in public speech.
senses.definitionZh: 尤指在公开讲话中礼貌或正式地称呼男性的方式；先生。
examples: The gentleman at the front has a question.
Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats.

entries.definition: A person who is invited to visit someone's home or attend an event; or a person staying at a hotel or similar place.
entries.definitionZh: 客人；宾客；住客；嘉宾
examples: We have a guest staying with us tonight.
The hotel offers free breakfast to its guests.
entries.tip: A guest is invited or received by a host; the host is the person who welcomes the guest.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to a visitor at a home or event, a hotel customer, or an invited participant.

senses.definition: A person invited to someone's home or to take part in an event.
senses.definitionZh: 受邀到某人家中或参加某项活动的人；客人或宾客。
examples: Each guest received a name badge.
We invited twenty guests to the wedding.

senses.definition: A person who pays to stay at a hotel or other accommodation.
senses.definitionZh: 付费入住酒店或其他住宿场所的人；住客。
examples: Hotel guests can use the swimming pool.
The guest checked out early.

senses.definition: A person invited to appear on a programme, speak at an event, or take part in an activity.
senses.definitionZh: 受邀在节目中露面、在活动中发言或参与某项活动的人；嘉宾。
examples: The show has a special guest tonight.
She was a guest speaker at the conference.

entries.definition: The father of someone's mother or father.
entries.definitionZh: 祖父；外祖父；爷爷；外公
examples: My grandfather taught me how to fish.
Her grandfather lives in a small village.
entries.tip: English “grandfather” does not distinguish the father's side from the mother's side; Chinese uses different terms.
entries.breakdown: A family relationship term for a parent's father.

senses.definition: The father of someone's mother or father.
senses.definitionZh: 某人的父亲或母亲的父亲；祖父或外祖父。
examples: My grandfather is eighty years old.
We visit our grandfather every weekend.

entries.definition: The mother of someone's mother or father.
entries.definitionZh: 祖母；外祖母；奶奶；外婆
examples: My grandmother makes excellent soup.
Their grandmother lives with the family.
entries.tip: English “grandmother” does not distinguish the father's side from the mother's side; Chinese uses different terms.
entries.breakdown: A family relationship term for a parent's mother.

senses.definition: The mother of someone's mother or father.
senses.definitionZh: 某人的父亲或母亲的母亲；祖母或外祖母。
examples: Her grandmother taught her to sew.
We called our grandmother on her birthday.
